caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1164 of 1998
lawyer:
MI Farooqui, Advocate instructed by MG Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record —For the Petitioner 
Not Represented —The Respondents.
parties:
Dr Fakir Anjuman Ara ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: Since the provision of section 4(b)(ii) of the Ordinance postulates a situation relating to taking over possession of a building distinctly different from the class of building specified in section 4(b)(i) of the Ordinance it cannot be said that discriminatory provision has been made for taking over possession of similar class of building ie abandoned building. Provision of section 4(b)(i) of the Ordinance relates to the class of building in respect whereof notice within the time specified in the said provision has already been issued and the provision of section 4(b)(ii) of the Ordinance relates to an abandoned property in respect whereof Government filed suit after the date that was specified in section 4(b)(i) of the Ordinance and as the provisions of section 4(b)(i) and 4(b) (ii) relate to two distinctly situated classes of abandoned building it cannot be said the provision of section 4(b)(ii) is discriminatory being violative of Article 27 of the Constitution. Mr Farooqui next submitted that the provision of section 5(2) of the Ordinance is bad in law since the same has saddled the claimant of the building in the list published under section 5(1) of the Ordinance with special burden of establishing that the building so listed as abandoned building is not an abandoned building but in the case of a person who is already in the civil Court prior to the promulgation of the Ordinance for the relief that the property is not an abandoned property has not been saddled with special burden of establishing that the property is not an abandoned property and consequently, the provision of section 5(2) of the Ordinance being discriminatory in respect of the persons placed at similar situation, the said provision of law is bad in law. He continues that the special burden of establishing that the building in the list published in the Official Gazette is not an abandoned building as has been provided in section 5(2) of the Ordinance is liable to be declared void being violative of Article 27 of the Constitution. The submission is not well founded in law in that the situation as has been contemplated in clause (a) to the proviso to section 5(1) of the Ordinance is quite different from the provision in section 5(2) of the Ordinance. Provision of section 5(2) of the Ordinance contemplates a situation as regard to a building, which has been listed as abandoned building in the list of the abandoned buildings published in the Official Gazette as per provision of section 5 of the Ordinance. The special onus with which a claimant of a property which has been listed as abandoned building in the Official Gazette published under section 5(1) of the Ordinance while he seeks remedy as against such listing before the court established under section 7 of the Ordinance for settlement of the claim that the property so listed is not an abandoned property, but the provision of clause (a) to the Proviso to section 5(1) relates to the class of suit or that in respect of the person of party in a suit who has gone before the civil Court prior to the promulgation of the Ordinance. So, the persons in the two types of proceedings, ie one which has been initiated by a person after the promulgation of the Ordinance before the Court of Settlement established under section 7 of the Ordinance and the other which has already been initialed before the civil Court relating to a building which has been treated as abandoned building before the promulgation of the Ordinance, undoubtedly belong not to the same class but to different classes. This being the position it in no way can be said that for the similar type of relief discrimination has been made by the provision of section 5(2) of the Ordinance in respect of similarly situated group of persons or same class of people. It is totally fallacious to say that the persons who have gone before the Court of Settlement after the publication of the list of abandoned buildings in the Official Gazette for seeking release of the property from the list so published in the Gazette and that the persons who prior to the promulgation of the Ordinance are already before the civil Court seeking declaration that the property or building is not an abandoned property or building are of the same class since the two groups are seeking relief in dissimilar situation or being placed in the situation at different times. By the provision of section 7 of the Ordinance special type of Court has been set up for the persons who are placed in similar situation ie whose buildings have been listed as abandoned buildings in the list published in the Official Gazette. If a person whose building has been listed as abandoned building in the list published in the Official Gazette intends to get the building released from the said list and approaches the court established under section 7 of the Ordinance, in that case he has been burdened with the special type of onus ie the property is not an abandoned property by the provisions of section 5(2) of the Ordinance. By the provision of section 5(2) of the Ordinance, statutory presumption has been created as to the character of the building so listed as being the abandoned building and that also as to the correctness of the list of the abandoned buildings published in the Official Gazette. In view of the said provision of law persons whose buildings have been listed in the list of abandoned buildings published in the Official Gazette have all equally been burdened with the special type of onus to establish that the buildings so listed in the list published in the Official Gazette are not abandoned buildings. All the persons whose buildings have been listed as abandoned buildings in the list published in the official Gazette being placed in the similar and equal situation it cannot be said that persons of the same group or position in similar situation have been discriminated by the provision of section 5(2) of the Ordinance.
